hypotheses.justification: The proof uses `hB` in only two places: `setIntegral_congr_ae (hB.prod measurableSet_Ioc)` inside `hleft` and inside `hright`. In both places the two integrands agree at every point, not only on the set. In `hleft`, the membership hypothesis `hqmem` is introduced and never used: the equality comes from `hτsymm`, `parabolicHomeomorph_symm_apply` and `buGaussian_timeShift_point_symm_apply`, all of which hold for every q. In `hright`, `τprod.symm (τprod q) = q` holds for every q (`simp`). So both calls can be replaced by `integral_congr_ae` with `filter_upwards [] with q` (or by `congr 1; funext q`), which needs no measurability of the set. The rest of the proof does not need it either. `MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_image_emb` (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/Set.lean:572) takes an arbitrary `s : Set X` because it uses a measurable embedding. `setIntegral_parabolic_to_product` takes arbitrary `Ω` and `I` with no measurability assumption. `himage`, `hτapply` and `hτsymm` are purely set-theoretic or algebraic. So the change of variables, and hence the theorem, holds for any `B ⊆ Vec3`.
